chapter: Freelance and studio work in New York
title: Arranging for Casa Loma and Fletcher Henderson at Connie's Inn
summary: He wrote and rehearsed arrangements for Casa Loma and Henderson, including My Gal Sal and Stardust, and recalls Henderson's sidemen.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: And then it became --
They were working one-nighters.
Then it became Glen Gray's -- later.
Not for a long while -- the Casa Loma they were out and they had their problems. You know, some of them wanted to quit. Business was bad. I think --
For everybody.

For everybody, but I had -- I was making arrangements for them, and I also made arrangements for Fletcher. He was up in Connie's Inn in Harlem and this is a nightclub job, a steady job and he was doing a couple extra -- making some recordings now and then so --
You used to go up to Connie's Inn to hear the band actually after you wrote the arrangements.
I also went up to hear them, not only that, I went up there to rehearse them. I went up there --
Who was in the band then, because I know the personnel had -- was Hawkins still there.
Hawkins was there. A fellow by the name of Boone, saxophone player.
Lester Boone?
(Harvey Boone -- ed.)
No, no. Boone, he was the alto player, he copied from a lot of Fletcher's arrangements. Boone and Buster. Well, Boone took Don Redman's place. That was it.
And then I don't Rex Stewart was there then. They got a little guy there --
Dick Vance, was he there?

No. This is a nice-looking little stark fellow and he played pretty good. Can't think -- Harrison was on trombone and then I think the guy from -- that used to be with the -- McKinney's Cotton Pickers, what's his name. With the toupee, played trombone. Clyde something.
Claude Jones.
Claude Jones. And I don't think Kayser Marshall was there.
What arrangements did you do for Fletcher, do you remember?

I did 'My Gal Sal,' I did a 'Stardust' for him. I had them all -- I think I might still have them downstairs. I did quite a number of them, but he got -- after he got out of there, he was having his problems. Everybody's beginning to have problems.
Now, this is what year, about 30 what.
'32, '33 around in there somewhere.
At the height of the Depression.
Right. Then, of course, with radio, Nat had about five shows.
So you were busy with that.
So I became busy with that. I worked for him for about three years.
